pinterest.title: Wedding Flowers in Season in Australia: Choose Your Date, Then Your Flowers
pinterest.description: Wedding flowers in season start with your date, not your mood board. Follow the Australian year season by season and month by month, with the questions to ask your florist for each one: what is fresh locally, how arrangements stay cool in summer, and what changes in the wet and dry seasons of the northern tropics. Save it for your first florist meeting.

pinterest.title: In Season or Imported Wedding Flowers? Questions to Ask Your Florist
pinterest.description: Local or imported wedding flowers? Imported cut flowers must meet Australian biosecurity import conditions, and that is your florist's work, not yours. Your part is a plain conversation: which stems are local and in season for your date, which come from overseas and when they are ordered, and what the backup is. Agree in writing which flowers are essential and which can be swapped.

pinterest.title: Destination Wedding Flowers: Why the Season Follows the Destination
pinterest.description: Marrying overseas? Your wedding flowers follow the destination's season, not Australia's. A June wedding at home falls in winter, while the same date in the northern hemisphere is summer. Ask a florist at the destination what is local, what is brought in and what the backup is, then get an itemised quote in writing. Leave the flowers from home behind.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Your wedding date decides your flowers more than your mood board does.

The month you marry shapes which stems are at their freshest, which will need to travel, and how much room your florist has to swap one stem for another if a crop comes in late. So set the date first, then settle the design.

A few things worth knowing:

Australia's seasons run opposite to the northern hemisphere's. Summer is December, January and February; winter is June, July and August. The northern tropics follow a wet and dry season instead.

Waratah flowering is concentrated in spring, so a spring wedding is the natural time to feature it, locally grown.

Imported cut flowers must meet Australian biosecurity import conditions. That is your florist's work, not yours. Your part is to ask which stems are local, which are imported, and what the backup is, and to agree in writing which flowers are essential.

Marrying abroad? The flowers follow the destination's season, so the florist there is the one to ask.
